text:
alex: Heads up -- noticed weird cross-request contamination on long contexts (>= 64k tokens) after the sliding-window GC landed. Samples show old KV pages being stitched into new responses.
anya: ack, can you paste a minimal repro/logs?
alex: repro steps below. ran a multi-session loop with prefix-reuse enabled + batch size 8. After ~3000 requests saw response drift where tokens from request N-2 appear in request N.
alex: logs snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T14:02:03Z] request=0x7f8c tag=rc123 page=45 slot=2 owner=req-312 lru=0x1f
[2026-03-15T14:02:03Z] request=0x7f8c tag=rc123 page=45 slot=2 read->kv.data[4096..8191]
[2026-03-15T14:02:03Z] request=0x8e9d tag=rc315 page=45 slot=2 owner=req-312 lru=0x3  <-- suspicious
```
jin: that looks like owner/request_id wasn't updated when page rotated. Could be a race between eviction and reuse path.
riley: also seen elevated cache-miss spikes right before contamination, maybe eviction was delayed and then rebind reused stale metadata.
anya: did kernel selection or batching changes touch page metadata path? The sliding-window GC touched the free-list and a fast-path for hot rebind.
alex: yes we added a fast rebind: when page.age < 2 and equiv size, do a blind reuse: `page->owner = cur_req` without full tag reset to avoid copying. Hypothesis: under concurrent batch completes, that mid-update leaves partial state.
infra-bot: deploy:staging reported increased kvcache-ops latency for node-7 between 14:00-14:10, correlation id f8a2c
jin: repro pretty reliably with stress harness and `--concurrent-batches=6 --enable-prefix-reuse`.
anya: temporary mitigation: flip off blind rebind and fall back to copy-on-rebind. Can we toggle via runtime flag?
alex: yes `kvcache.rebind_fastpath=false` is safe and prevents the repro instantly.
riley: we should add an assertion in debug builds to catch partial resets, something like:
```
assert(page->owner == NO_OWNER || page->tag == expected_tag);
```
jin: also want to add a unit test that simulates eviction competing with reuse: GC thread runs while batch retires.
anya: I'll file a short RFC and a canary patch. plan:
- patch: disable fastpath by default + add invariant checks (alex)
- tests: deterministic GC/rebind race test (jin)
- perf: rerun kernel/batching perf sweep to see regression (riley)
- ship canary to staging (anya)
alex: assigned. I'll push PR with patch + repro harness.
riley: note: this fix adds ~2% p99 latency on small tokens due to extra copy. We'll measure with perf harness and explore targeted copy avoidance.
anya: long term idea: make per-page generation counters (64-bit) instead of owner pointer flip so we can atomically bump generation and avoid stale views. That avoids full copy in many cases.
jin: agree, gen counters + seqnum compare would be cleaner. Add to perf backlog.
alex: thanks everyone. I'll post PR link when ready and update on canary results.
riley: :thumbsup:
infra-bot: canary deploy started on staging cluster at 2026-03-15T15:10:00Z (canary id c-2026-03-15-1510)
anya: tagging the runtime-oncall to keep eyes on it during canary: @riley
alex: quick note for release notes: "fix: prevent KV page reuse race causing cross-request token leakage on long contexts" — need legal/SE review if any customer-facing disclosure required.
anya: filing incident tracker placeholder just in case: INC-2026-042
alex: ok closing thread for now, will reopen if canary shows issues.
